article_title: Bylaw 14842 — Pay Parking and Electric Vehicle Charging Bylaw 2026
body:

Page 1 of 9 
 
 
CITY OF BURNABY 
BYLAW NO. 14842 
A BYLAW respecting pay parking and 
electric vehicle charging on City lands 
 
The Council of the City of Burnaby ENACTS as follows: 
PART 1: CITATION 
1.1 
This bylaw may be cited as BURNABY PAY PARKING AND ELECTRIC 
VEHICLE CHARGING BYLAW 2026. 
PART 2: INTERPRETATION 
2.1 
In this bylaw: 
“bylaw” 
means this bylaw, including all schedules attached hereto 
 
“City” 
means the City of Burnaby 
 
“electric vehicle” 
means any vehicle that operates, either partially or 
exclusively, on electrical energy from an off-board source, 
that is stored on-board for motive purposes, but for the 
purposes of this bylaw, does not include vehicles that cannot 
be licensed by the Insurance Corporation of British Columbia 
 
 
“electric vehicle 
charging meter” 
means a battery charging station with a specified nominal 
power output of less than 24 kW for Level 2 and up to 350 
kW for Level 3 that is available for public use for the purpose 
of transferring electric energy (by conductive or inductive 
means) to a battery or other energy storage device in an 
electric vehicle, installed in an electric vehicle metered zone 
pursuant to this bylaw for the purpose of identifying a parking 
space as an electric vehicle metered space  
 
“electric vehicle 
metered space” 
means any marked parking space that identified the use to be 
exclusively for the charging of an electric vehicle and for 
which an electric vehicle charging meter has been installed 
pursuant to this bylaw 
 
“electric vehicle 
metered zone” 
means any portion of City-owned lands designated as an 
electric vehicle metered zone as set out in Schedule “A” of 
this bylaw 

Bylaw No. 14842 
Page 2 of 9 
 
 
“General Manager 
Engineering”  
means the head of the City’s Engineering Department, or 
designate 
 
“motorcycle”  
means a motorized vehicle that runs on two wheels 
 
“park” 
means the stopping or standing of a vehicle, whether occupied 
or not 
 
“parking meter” 
means a mechanical, electronic or automatic device installed 
in a pay parking zone pursuant to this bylaw for the purposes 
of identifying a pay parking space and, where payment is 
made to the parking meter, measuring and indicating the 
time during which a vehicle may be parked in a pay parking 
space  
 
 
“pay-by-phone 
system” 
 
means a telecommunications system approved by the City for 
accepting the payment of the fee for parking a vehicle in a 
pay parking space and measuring the time during which a 
vehicle may be parked in a pay parking space 
 
“pay parking signage”  
 
means a sign identifying a portion of a pay parking zone as 
pay parking spaces 
 
“pay parking space”  
 
 
  
means a portion of a street, within a pay parking zone, that 
requires payment in accordance with section 5.1 of this bylaw 
prior to parking a vehicle on that portion of the street, as 
designated by pay parking signage or a parking meter 
 
“pay parking zone” 
 
means a part of the City identified in dotted black lines and 
designated as a pay parking zone in Schedule “B” of this 
bylaw 
 
“pay station” 
 
means a device installed within a pay parking zone, for 
accepting payment in accordance with section 5.1 of this 
bylaw for parking a vehicle in a pay parking space 
 
“shared vehicle” 
means a four-wheeled automobile, van, or pick-up truck 
owned and operated by a shared vehicle organization  
 
“shared vehicle decal” 
 
means a decal issued by the City, following payment of the 
shared vehicle decal fee set out in the Burnaby Consolidated 
Fees and Charges Bylaw, identifying a vehicle as a shared 
vehicle 
 

Bylaw No. 14842 
Page 3 of 9 
 
“shared vehicle 
organization” 
means a legal entity: 
 
(a) 
whose principal business objective is to provide its 
members, for a fee, with a car-sharing service by 
which such members have access to a fleet of 
shared vehicles which they may reserve for use on 
an hourly basis; and 
 
(b) 
which has a valid agreement with the City to 
authorize the shared vehicle organization to 
allow its members to park its shared vehicles on 
a City street 
 
“vehicle” 
means a device in, on or by which a person or thing is or may 
be transported or drawn on a street or highway, except a 
device designed to be moved by human power or used 
exclusively on stationary rails or tracks, and includes a 
motorcycle and an electric vehicle 
 
PART 3: DELEGATIONS  
3.1 
The General Manager Engineering is hereby authorized and delegated the authority to: 
(a) 
designate pay parking spaces within pay parking zones;  
(b) 
designate electric vehicle metered spaces within electric vehicle metered zones; 
(c) 
cause the installation and maintenance of pay parking signage, parking meters 
and pay stations in respect to pay parking spaces; 
(d) 
cause the installation and maintenance of electric vehicle charging meters in 
respect to electric vehicle metered spaces; and 
(e) 
establish rules and regulations in respect to pay parking spaces and electric 
vehicle metered spaces, including without limiting the generality of the foregoing: 
(i) 
the rate to be paid for parking in a pay parking space or charging an 
electric vehicle in an electric vehicle metered space, subject to the 
maximum rates set out in the Burnaby Consolidated Fees and Charges 
Bylaw; 
(ii) 
the hours during which payment is required for a pay parking space; 
(iii) 
the maximum consecutive period for either the parking of a vehicle in a 
pay parking space or the charging of an electric vehicle in an electric 
vehicle metered space; and  

Bylaw No. 14842 
Page 4 of 9 
 
(iv) 
the size or type of vehicle permitted to be parked in a pay parking space 
or electric vehicle metered space. 
3.2 
The General Manager Engineering may temporarily discontinue the use of a pay 
parking space for the parking of vehicles or the use of an electric vehicle metered space 
for the charging of electric vehicles and may place at such space a sign indicating that 
parking or charging, as applicable, is not permitted at that space and no person shall park 
a vehicle or charge an electric vehicle, as applicable, in such space while such sign is so 
placed. 
3.3 
The City is hereby authorized and empowered, through its employees and/or contactors, 
to remove, detain or impound any vehicle, chattel or obstruction unlawfully occupying any 
portion of a pay parking space or electric vehicle metered space, and to recover all costs 
and expenses incurred thereby either from the owner of the vehicle, chattel or obstruction, 
or by the sale of the vehicle, chattel or obstruction. Whenever any vehicle, chattel or 
obstruction is removed, detained or impounded pursuant to this bylaw, the owner of said 
vehicle, chattel or obstruction shall pay all costs and expenses incurred thereby, including 
storage costs. 
PART 4: PAY PARKING AND ELECTRIC VEHICLE PARKING  
4.1 
Except as provided in section 4.2 of this bylaw, no person shall park more than one vehicle 
in a pay parking space or an electric vehicle metered space. 
4.2 
Not more than three motorcycles may be parked in a pay parking space. 
4.3 
No person shall park or permit a vehicle to remain parked in a pay parking space: 
(a) 
unless payment has been made in accordance with section 5.1 of this bylaw and 
the period of time for which payment has been made has not expired; or 
(b) 
for a period of time which exceeds the maximum consecutive period established 
by the General Manager Engineering for the pay parking space pursuant to 
section 3.1(e)(iii) of this bylaw. 
4.4 
No person shall park or permit an electric vehicle to remain parked in an electric vehicle 
metered space: 
(a) 
unless payment has been made in respect to charging the electric vehicle in the 
electric vehicle metered space; or 
(b) 
if the electric vehicle is not actively charging from an electric vehicle charging 
meter; or

minutes_briefs.title: Burnaby's new pay parking and EV charging bylaw gives City power to set rates and tow violators
minutes_briefs.summary: Burnaby has passed a new bylaw (No. 14842) that sets the rules for paid parking and electric vehicle (EV) charging on City-owned land. The bylaw gives the City's Engineering department the power to create paid parking zones, set parking rates and time limits, and install EV charging stations. It also allows the City to tow, impound, or sell any vehicle parked illegally in these spaces, and to charge the owner for all costs. Drivers must pay before parking in a pay space, and EV drivers must be actively charging their vehicle while parked in an EV-only charging spot.
minutes_briefs.action_required: Review your parking and EV charging policies to ensure they comply with the new bylaw's rules on payment, time limits, and towing.
